blocks.prompt: 15 (a) A locker of a bank is locked with four letters (A-Z). How many different passwords can be generated if: (a) repetition of the alphabets is allowed
blocks.explanation:
A password is an ordered string: ABCD and DCBA are different passwords. Letters may repeat.
We must count 4-letter passwords from 26 letters.
Plan: 4 places, each with 26 choices: \(26^{4}\).
steps:
Given: 26 letters A to Z; password of 4 letters; repetition allowed.
To find: the number of passwords.
Method: Fundamental principle of counting: fill 4 places one after another and multiply the choices.

Count the choices for each place
\[26 \times 26 \times 26 \times 26\]
Why: A letter used once can be used again, so every place still has all 26 letters.

Check
\[676 \times 676 = 676 \times 700 - 676 \times 24\]
\[= 473200 - 16224 = 456976 \;\checkmark\]
Why: A second way of multiplying gives the same number.

blocks.prompt: 15 (b) A locker of a bank is locked with four letters (A-Z). How many different passwords can be generated if: (b) repetition of the alphabets is not allowed
blocks.explanation:
Again order matters (it is a password), but now all 4 letters must be different.
We must count the arrangements of 4 letters out of 26.
Plan: \({}^{26}P_{4} = 26 \times 25 \times 24 \times 23\).
steps:
Given: 26 letters; 4-letter password; no letter repeated.
To find: the number of passwords.
Method: Ordered and without repetition, so this is a permutation \({}^{n}P_{r}\) with \(n = 26\), \(r = 4\).

Count the choices place by place
\[26 \times 25 \times 24 \times 23\]
Why: Each letter used cannot be used again, so each next place has one letter fewer.

Multiply
\[26 \times 25 = 650\]
\[650 \times 24 = 15600\]
\[15600 \times 23 = 358800\]
Why: Multiply two at a time.

Check
\[{}^{26}P_{4} = \dfrac{26!}{22!} = 26 \cdot 25 \cdot 24 \cdot 23\]
\[358800 < 456976 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The formula gives the same product, and forbidding repeats must give fewer passwords than part (a).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints (i) 358,800 and (ii) 14,950. 358,800 is the answer to part (b), not (a); 14,950 \(= {}^{26}C_{4}\) is a combination, which is wrong for a password because the order of the letters matters. Correct: (a) \(26^{4} = 456{,}976\); (b) \({}^{26}P_{4} = 358{,}800\).
